synthesis.body: git's die()/error() strings are gettext msgids wrapped in _(), so a build with translation catalogues installed prints them in the user's language. A script that branches on 'couldn't find remote ref' (or any other English wording) silently stops firing on such a machine — and the fallback branch is usually the generic one, so it fails quietly rather than loudly. Set LC_ALL=C in the subprocess env before matching. GNU gettext ignores LANGUAGE when the locale is C, so LC_ALL alone is enough. Apple Git ships no catalogues, so this is invisible on macOS.

title: Classifying a git failure by its message needs LC_ALL=C
